transcript.content: Hello, what brings you in today?

Well, I came in because... I keep catching myself thinking that it might just be easier if I didn't wake up. I haven't made any plans to hurt myself or anything like that, but... yeah, those thoughts are just there, and I figured I should probably come in and talk to someone about it.
Have you ever had a distinct period when you felt unusually elevated or unusually irritable compared with your normal self?

Yeah, actually. Right after I got fired from my last job, I didn't feel down about it right away. Instead, I felt oddly fired up. I just had this feeling like I was going to prove everybody wrong. But at the same time, I was also really on edge. I remember snapping at people over just little things, like the barista at the coffee shop. It was definitely different from how I normally am.
How long did that unusually fired-up and irritable period last?
I'd say it lasted for about three weeks. Yeah, that whole high-energy, kind of out-of-control stretch went on for right around three weeks after I got fired.
During that three-week period, did you need less sleep than usual without feeling tired?

Yeah, I did. There were actually several nights where I only slept for maybe two or three hours. But I didn't feel tired at all. I'd get up feeling like I had a full tank, you know? Just completely ready to go, with no reason to slow down.
Did you need to be hospitalized because of that unusually energized and irritable period?
No, I didn't go to the hospital or anything like that. I mean, I was definitely wound up, but it wasn't like I needed to be admitted. I just sort of rode it out at home.
During that three-week period, were you using any alcohol, recreational drugs, or new medications?
No, I wasn't. I mean, I don't really drink much anyway, and I definitely wasn't using any drugs. As for medications, it was just my usual stuff, nothing new. So, no, nothing like that.
Have you ever had a period lasting at least two weeks when you felt depressed or lost interest in most things nearly every day?

Yeah, I have. After that burst of energy wore off, it was like somebody had just pulled the plug on me. That lasted for a few weeks, at least. I'd just sit at the table in the mornings, staring at my coffee... not wanting to go into work or do much of anything. I just felt completely empty, and honestly, pretty ashamed. It was like that pretty much every day.
During that three-week period, did your energized and irritable state cause severe problems in your work, relationships, or ability to function day to day?

Yeah, it did. I mean, I couldn't keep up with much of anything. I fell way behind on my bills, and I was missing callbacks and appointments. I really needed to find work, but I just couldn't keep a steady job search going. Even my usual routines around the house got pretty sloppy. It got to the point where I knew I couldn't just fix it with willpower, you know? It was definitely messing up my day-to-day life.
During that energized and irritable period, did you ever hear or see things that others could not, or strongly believe things that others said were not true?

Yeah, I did. It was... well, when I was all wound up like that, I actually heard my old store manager's voice. It was clear as day, like it was coming over a store intercom, telling me to "move the display." But the thing is, I was just sitting all alone in my kitchen when it happened. So, yeah, I was definitely hearing things that weren't there.
Have you ever heard voices or had unusual beliefs during a time when you were neither depressed nor unusually energized or irritable?

No, I haven't. The only time I heard that manager's voice... or had those ideas about being able to take over any store... that was just during those few weeks when I was all wired up after losing my job. Once that energy ran out and I hit that low spell, the voice went away completely. I was just left feeling pretty embarrassed about the things I'd been thinking. But no, when I'm feeling normal, I don't hear or believe anything like that.
